instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on until you serve.
Slice the chicken across the grain into strips about 1/4 inch thick. Transfer it to a bowl and mix in 1 tsp of the cornstarch, 1 tsp soy sauce and 1 tsp of the oil. Leave it for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim the snow peas and mince the 2 garlic cloves.
In a small bowl, stir the remaining 2 tsp cornstarch into the chicken broth until smooth.
In a second small bowl, stir together 1 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1/2 tsp sesame oil, the salt, the white pepper and a pinch of sugar.

Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until it's smoking. Add 1 tbsp of the oil and half the chicken in a single layer. Leave it alone for 1 minute, until the underside is browned. Transfer it to a plate, then repeat with 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the chicken.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Add the garlic and snow peas and stir for 1 minute, until the peas turn bright green.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Pour in the soy sauce mixture and stir for 15 seconds.
Stir the broth mixture again and pour it in. Cook for 30 to 45 seconds, until the sauce coats a spoon.
You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick slice. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink left.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: The lead (The Woks of Life, 4.95 from 38) sears thin marinated chicken first, then stir-fries the snow peas briefly with garlic, adds the seasonings, and thickens a light stock sauce. This is scaled to 1 lb of chicken and a pound of peas for four, with a bit more stock for a spoonable sauce, and the chicken seared in two batches so it browns. The 10 minute marinade runs while the rice cooks, so the whole dish takes about 20 minutes.
